findings.reason: Keeping only the latest message reference can suppress a legitimate notification for an earlier readable reply when the newest reply is private, although the permission floor permits a generic notice backed by any currently readable reply and a context-aware choice among verified candidates could preserve that benefit.

findings.standard: An Instar Agent Is Always a Multi-Machine Entity
findings.reason: A disconnected push holder can read an older unmuted value as current and send after another machine acknowledges mute, and the draft establishes no basis for extending the Conversations Pending exception to personal preference changes.

findings.standard: Maturation Path — Test Agent → Development Agent → Fleet
findings.reason: The graduation criterion accepts “meaningful three-tier checks” and native proof without defining a machine-checkable outcome for each rung, such as evidence that a queued muted reply was suppressed while an authorized notice was delivered.

The opening relies on “Chief,” a handoff identifier, and a frozen PR before explaining how conversation lists and reply notifications work today, leaving an independent reader to reconstruct the context for the change.

fit.reason: A durable mute or archive choice spares the reader repeated interruptions or list clutter, but the spec identifies no recurring defect caused by a structure that people must continually maintain through attention.
